clue.text: Latest news on University head adopting daughter

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the head takes the daughter inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A news bulletin about a college principal who has adopted a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside PATE to make PDATE, with U placed before it to give UPDATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is a fresh report bringing someone current with the most recent developments.

clue.text: Dress in York lifted up

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ebor, from the Latin Eboracum, is the traditional abbreviation for York, used by its archbishop

explanation.surface: Someone in York dressed in clothes hoisted up off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: EBOR read upwards gives ROBE. The Ebor is also a famous horse race at York.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment, and both words can be nouns for an item of clothing.

clue.text: A reminder to carry on with wine

parts.note: to keep doing something is to carry on with it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A nudge to keep drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small memento kept to bring back memories of a person or occasion.

clue.text: A guide is key to crossing river from the South

parts.note: the Escape key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards turns the letters round
one word crossing another lies across it, so it goes round the river

parts.note: taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Advice that the essential thing for a guide is getting across a river heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'from the South' means read from the bottom, so only the river-crossing part is turned round; the key stays first.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort accompanies and leads someone, acting as a guide or protector on the way.

clue.text: Rocking 'n' rolling, jive until the start of your adolescence

indicators.note: rocking and rolling moves things about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Teenagers dancing rock 'n' roll until youth begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance-floor picture fits the definition, but jive until plus Y is the letter supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenility is the state of being young, and adolescence is that youthful stage of life.

clue.text: Slashes blouse fashioned to include measure of brilliance

indicators.note: the reworked garment takes the measure inside itself
something fashioned is shaped anew, so the letters are remade in another order

parts.note: taken as written
IQ, the intelligence quotient, measures how clever someone is

explanation.surface: Someone slashes a blouse, cut to show off a clever design.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOUSE is rearranged to OBLUES and IQ is set in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliques is a name for the slanting punctuation marks also called slashes or strokes.

clue.text: Zero pressure working in the midst of confined enemy

indicators.note: being in the midst of something means sitting inside it

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
P is the symbol for pressure in physics
pent, as in pent-up, means shut in
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: No pressure working among a hemmed-in foe.
explanation.walkthrough: Pent survives mainly in pent-up, meaning shut in or held back.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone who stands against you in a contest or fight, a rival or foe.

clue.text: Couple eating a dry Scots vegetable

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside

parts.note: to couple things is to tie them together
taken as written
TT, teetotal, describes someone who does not drink

explanation.surface: A pair sitting down to a plain Scottish vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means not drinking alcohol, the teetotal sense, not lacking moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattie is the Scottish word for a potato, the common root vegetable.

clue.text: Small and fat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short, like a stub

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a stocky figure, but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubby describes something both short in length and thick in girth, like stubby fingers.

clue.text: Flatten flatfish, so it's said

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the spelling goes by sound

parts.note: rays are flat cartilaginous fish such as skates

explanation.surface: A joke that flattening a fish makes a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: To raze a building is to demolish it completely, levelling it to the ground.

clue.text: Eating chop unfortunately causing illness

indicators.note: something that went unfortunately went wrong, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eating a bad pork chop made someone sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathogenic describes germs or agents capable of producing disease in a host.

clue.text: It's essential for seeing part of minaret in Alhambra

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across minaRET IN Alhambra

explanation.surface: A tourist's must-see: a tower at the Alhambra palace in Granada.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, without which there is no vision.

clue.text: Perk up in Spanish city, and tear off

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: Vigo is a port city in Galicia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone livened up in a Spanish city, then rushed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear off' looks like a phrase meaning dash away, but off is the anagram signal working on tear.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate is to give energy and life to someone, which is to liven or perk them up.

clue.text: Popular US soldier sent back in genuine conspiracy

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the soldier sits in the word for genuine

parts.note: true means real or genuine

indicators.note: sending a soldier back means his letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: GI is the standard term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A well-liked American serviceman returned home amid a real plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' reads as a soldier posted home, but it turns the soldier's letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrigue is a secret scheme or plot, the same thing as a conspiracy.

clue.text: Socialist struggle inspired by boozer

indicators.note: what is inspired is breathed in, so the struggle goes inside the drinker

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A left-wing fight fired up by a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer here is the drinker, not the British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Soviet is used as an adjective for the communist, and so socialist, state of the former USSR.

clue.text: Servant's opening can of silvery American fish

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
a tin is a can
gray is the American spelling of grey, the silvery colour

explanation.surface: A servant opening a tin of shiny American fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a venomous barbed tail.

clue.text: Notices filling of best 17D

indicators.note: the filling is what lies inside, the middle letters of the word

parts.note: the middle letters of the word
17-down is pastries, and pies are pastries

explanation.surface: Someone spots the filling in the finest strudels.
explanation.walkthrough: 17D stands for that clue's answer word pastries, whose synonym supplies the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy something is to catch sight of it, so espies means spots or notices.

clue.text: Rinds of sweet lemons covering basic pastries

indicators.note: the kept letters cover, so they wrap round the next word
the rind is the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
rude means primitive or basic, as in rude shelter
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Candied lemon peel tops simple pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pairs of outer letters act as one wrapper, split around the middle word.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudels are pastries of thin layered dough rolled round a filling, often apple.

clue.text: Band of forgers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Manchester indie group of Morrissey and Johnny Marr
second meaning: workers who forge metal

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gang of counterfeiters, but forgers here shape iron at a forge, not fake cheques.
explanation.definitionFit: The Smiths were a famous 1980s rock group, and metalworkers who forge iron at an anvil are also called this.

clue.text: Doctor wrong to get involved in lip disorder

indicators.note: getting involved in something means going inside it

parts.note: the lip of a cup is its rim

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic wrongly meddling with someone's lip condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'disorder' make a medical scene, but doctor is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a contagious fungal skin condition, an ailment or disorder of the skin.

clue.text: Newspapers' eyes and ears?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: publications that speak for a party or group
second meaning: body parts that perform functions, here the sense parts

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like reporters, the press's eyes and ears, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper voicing a group's views, and eyes and ears are examples of the body's sense organs.

clue.text: Relinquish yacht helm altogether on vacation time

indicators.note: vacated words have emptied out, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters
the first and last letters
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Giving up sailing completely while away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, time and rhythm both mean the regular beat or pattern of a piece.

clue.text: Box of fizz unwrapped

indicators.note: unwrapping takes off the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: champers is British slang for champagne

explanation.surface: A case of bubbly with the paper taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne; drop its outer C and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large basket or box, often for food and drink.

clue.text: Collected a horse barrier in crimson

indicators.note: the barrier is placed in the colour word

parts.note: taken as written
gee-gee, a child's word for a horse
crimson is a shade of red
a gate is a barrier in a fence

explanation.surface: Someone gathered a horse and a fence in red.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse, a common crossword source of GG.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregated means gathered together into a whole, the same as collected.

clue.text: Reminder — the writer of this puzzle takes a little time

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
mo, short for moment, is a short while

explanation.surface: A note that the setter takes a while over the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note to jog someone's memory.

clue.text: Piece of trim in Italian car

indicators.note: a piece is a fragment, a short run of letters taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across triM IN Italian

explanation.surface: A bit of decorative trim inside an Italian sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian car' looks like the definition, but Italian only holds the final letter; the car is British.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a small British car, first made in 1959.

clue.text: Alien ignoring second appearance of a bird

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out

parts.note: a Martian is a creature from Mars
the second time the letter a appears in the word

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial overlooking a second sighting of something.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTIAN has two As; dropping the second leaves MARTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The martin is a small swallow-like bird, such as the house martin.

clue.text: Author's one to stick around after show starts

indicators.note: after tells us the one and the hanging about follow the opening letter rather than preceding it
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
a means one
to linger is to hang about

explanation.surface: A writer's urge to hang about after a performance begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author's' reads as possessive but is author is, a definition plus link.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger was the American novelist who wrote The Catcher in the Rye.
